wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/add_glob_flags.py: """`glob()` declared no `$flags` parameter, so every flagged call was a compile error.

    glob("d/*", GLOB_ONLYDIR);
    → error: glob() takes exactly 1 argument

The runtime already calls libc `glob()` — with the flags hard-coded to ZERO. Most of php's flags
are the libc ones and only have to be forwarded: `GLOB_MARK` appends `/` to directories,
`GLOB_NOSORT` leaves filesystem order, `GLOB_NOCHECK` answers the pattern itself when nothing
matched, `GLOB_NOESCAPE`, `GLOB_BRACE` and `GLOB_ERR` likewise. MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6, one
flag at a time.

`GLOB_ONLYDIR` is php's OWN bit, not libc'
